chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdullah from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Lu'lu'i, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughira al-Nasri and Umar ibn Hanzala, from Mansur ibn Hazim, they said:

We used to measure the sun in Medina using the cubit. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to us, 'Shall I not inform you of something clearer than this?' We said, 'Yes, may Allah make us your ransom.' He said, 'When the sun passes its zenith, the time for Dhuhr prayer has entered, except that there is a 'subhah' (period of voluntary prayer) before it, and that is up to you. If you shorten your subhah, then when you finish your subhah, and if you lengthen it, then when you finish your subhah.'

And no one should say, 'How can you act upon these hadiths given the difference in their wording and the apparent contradiction in their meanings?' Because some of them mention the height of a person (qamah), some mention the cubit (dhirah), and some mention the foot (qadam). These are different measurements. For although the words differ, the meanings are not different.

One reason is that we have clarified that when the sun passes its zenith, the time for Dhuhr has entered, except for the one who prays the voluntary subhah prayer. The prayer of subhah varies according to the variation of the pray-ers. So whoever prays for the time it takes for the sun to reach the height of a foot, that is his time. And whoever prays for the time it takes to reach a cubit, that is his time then. And whoever prays until the sun reaches the height of a person, that is his time.

And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) explicitly stated this in the hadith we mentioned earlier from Mansur ibn Hazim, from his words, 'Shall I not inform you of something clearer than this?' Then he said, 'When the sun passes its zenith, the time for Dhuhr has entered, except that there is a subhah before it. If you shorten it, then when you finish from it, and if you lengthen it, then when you finish from it.'

The second is that all that these narrations included regarding the mention of the height (qamah) and the cubit (dhirah), the intended meaning is the cubit. And they (peace be upon them) clarified that, and it was narrated.

key_terms.السُّبْحَة: A period of voluntary prayer before the obligatory prayer
key_terms.الْقَامَة: The height of a standing person

ai.seo_question: When exactly does the time for Dhuhr prayer begin according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi uses this narration from Imam al-Sadiq to resolve the apparent contradiction between hadiths citing specific physical measurements (cubit, foot) and those relying on the sun's zenith, establishing that the 'subhah' (voluntary prayer) duration is relative to the individual's pace. This scholarly interpretation emphasizes flexibility in fiqh, where the obligatory Dhuhr time begins only after the person completes their variable-length voluntary prayer, thereby harmonizing differing textual reports. It highlights the Shia method of reconciling narrations by distinguishing between literal measurements and the practical, time-based reality of worship.
